items.title: Live: US accuses Iran of 'economic terrorism' over Strait of Hormuz obstruction as blockade begins
items.description: US Vice-President JD Vance accuses the Iranian government of engaging in "economic terrorism" by blocking traffic through the Strait of Hormuz as the US Navy begins its blockade of the key shipping waterway. Follow live.

items.title: Global food crisis warning, accusations of Hormuz piracy as the blockade begins
items.description: The fragile truce in the Middle East and the situation in the Strait of Hormuz have dire consequences for the rest of the world.

items.title: Breaking: Qantas cuts domestic flights and raises fares as fuel costs blow out
items.description: Qantas will cut domestic flights due to higher fuel costs and the uncertainty of the Middle East war, as it flags as much as $800 million in extra fuel costs.

items.title: Safety alert issued amid explosion of illegal peptide use
items.description: The medicines regulator issues a health alert about the risks of using unregulated peptides amid a surge in the use of potentially unsafe injectables.

items.title: Live: Australia to join UK, France at summit on Strait of Hormuz
items.description: Australia will join more than 40 nations to discuss safeguarding shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, Labor's Pat Conroy has confirmed. Follow live.

items.title: Debunking four myths about Australia's fuel crisis
items.description: If you listen to increasingly shrill calls, it is time to rebuild our oil industry. While the sentiments might be well-meant, a few unfortunate facts have been overlooked.

items.title: Ex-One Nation candidate wants Hanson 'held accountable' for rehiring rapist ex-staffer
items.description: Two former One Nation candidates have accused party leader Pauline Hanson and chief of staff James Ashby of dismissing concerns raised internally about the convicted rapist and former campaign director Sean Black.

items.title: As the Sussexes return to Australia, 'unusual' commercial engagements are raising eyebrows
items.description: Harry and Meghan will be travelling under their titles of Duke and Duchess of Sussex, and will appear at two major, ticketed events as well as making the rounds of various charities and causes.

items.title: Trump's 'AI Jesus' post sparks backlash as pope responds to attack
items.description: Donald Trump is criticised by religious sections of his supporter base after publishing, then deleting, the image, but the US president says: "I thought it was me as a doctor."

items.title: Why Gout's incredible run deserves equal measures of praise and patience
items.description: Gout Gout was on the lips of every athletics fan across the globe on the weekend, but elements of his record-breaking run need to be treated with caution.

items.title: Fiji Police are circling an Australian wanted over four-tonne meth import
items.description: Key insiders from Fiji's largest-ever meth bust say the drug import had alarming links to organised crime in Australia.

items.title: Live: Stocks rally, oil prices retreat on hopes of US-Iran deal
items.description: As the US Navy blockade of Iranian ports begins, stocks rise and oil prices retreat. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Roblox to launch accounts for children after grooming claims
items.description: Roblox will launch restricted accounts for children and teenagers, two months after being put on notice by the government over reports children were being groomed on the platform.

items.title: 'Make a noise': The ordinary people who took their fight to our highest court
items.description: From love and freedom to native title and the right to vote, these are some of the High Court cases that have helped define our nation, and the ordinary people behind them.

items.title: How these queer couples split the mental load might surprise you
items.description: After publishing our story on the four stages of the mental load, we asked to hear from queer couples about how they divide and conquer the cognitive and emotional labour at home.

items.title: The neuroscience behind synaesthesia paints a surprising inner world
items.description: Have you ever tasted a word, or seen colours while listening to music? If you have, you may be among the 1 to 4 per cent of people who have a fascinating trait known as synaesthesia.

items.title: Kitty Flanagan and Anne Edmonds create comedy chaos in new show
items.description: Plus Nicole Kidman is an Aussie wrestler in Margo's Got Money Troubles, Baby Reindeer's Richard Gadd returns, and the reboots keep on coming with Malcolm in the Middle.

items.title: Starc honoured as Wisden slams England's 'feckless' Ashes
items.description: Australia's Ashes ace Mitchell Starc is named the leading men's cricketer of the year by the Wisden Cricketers' Almanack after taking 55 wickets in 2025.

items.title: Sydney summers are now hotter and nearly 50 days longer, study finds
items.description: For every 10 years since 1990, Sydneysiders have experienced an extra 15 days of summer, new research has found.

items.title: Beijing is shifting its Taiwan strategy. Here is why
items.description: It began with a dish once served to Nixon in 1971. Now Beijing is using the same stage to reshape the Taiwan question. China is advancing a slower strategy: using economic incentives and political engagement to influence Taiwan's future.

items.title: Trail mix and water help 87yo woman survive near-freezing night in dense forest
items.description: Police say the woman wandered down a rabbit track after becoming disoriented on a weekend bushwalk.

items.title: Banks raise 300 red flags in five months on illicit tobacco activity
items.description: Australia's big banks have made hundreds of reports of suspicious activity related to illegal tobacco since the anti-money laundering regulator called for a crackdown late last year.

items.title: How Sydney's underworld is breaking a once unspoken rule
items.description: Sydney's underworld used to operate by a code, but those unspoken rules have come undone. In today's gangland wars, violence is spilling into suburbia, and anyone can become collateral damage.

items.title: Bomb squad called in after rental home cleaner finds explosives, drugs, cash
items.description: Authorities were forced to conduct controlled explosions at a property in Melbourne's north-west after a cleaner stumbled across drugs and explosives.

items.title: Teenager 'begging' minister to deport abuser who had visa reinstated
items.description: A girl who was sexually assaulted in Perth by a UK citizen when she was nine years old writes to Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke, pleading with him to cancel the man's visa after he avoided deportation on appeal.
